title: Necessary But Not Sufficient
sensory_anchor: the condition that opens nothing by itself
body: {person} argued that since {necessary_condition}, therefore {conclusion}. They were right that {necessary_condition} was needed. But it wasn't enough — {what_else_was_needed} was also required. The confusion between necessary and sufficient led them to {wrong_conclusion}. Seeing the gap was the whole thing.

title: If-Then, But Not Then-If
sensory_anchor: the arrow pointing one direction only
emotional_signature: the satisfaction of catching a subtle fallacy
body: The claim was: if {antecedent}, then {consequent}. True. But then someone argued: so if {consequent}, then {antecedent}. That's the converse fallacy. {antecedent} is sufficient for {consequent}, but {consequent} doesn't prove {antecedent}. The correct contrapositive is: if not {consequent}, then not {antecedent}. Caught it because {caught_reason}.

title: The Assumption They Needed
sensory_anchor: the wobble when you push on it
body: The argument worked IF you accepted {hidden_assumption}. Nobody stated it. It wasn't obviously false. But it wasn't obviously true either, and the entire structure depended on it. {person} didn't realize they were building on air. When I pointed out the assumption, {their_reaction}. The argument wasn't wrong — it was incomplete in a way that happened to serve {whose_interest}.
